powerdock.ponder.catenary_hanger.text_1: Aim at a rail and right-click with a hanger. The assembly snaps four blocks above the track.
powerdock.ponder.catenary_hanger.text_2: You can aim partway through a curve or incline. The crossbeam turns across the track at that point.
powerdock.ponder.catenary_hanger.text_3: Look for the highlighted rail. Sneak-right-click it with an empty hand to open Hanger Settings.
powerdock.ponder.catenary_hanger.text_5: Mount starts on Floating. Build a support up to the short crosspiece, or choose a mount in Hanger Settings.
powerdock.ponder.catenary_hanger.text_6: Choose Cantilever pole and select a side. Reach moves the foot. A square portal has a separate reach for each foot.
powerdock.ponder.catenary_hanger.text_7: Right-click exposed steel with a Power Grid Wire Connector, even on a brace. Wire each conductor through its own fittings to the matching head terminal.
powerdock.ponder.catenary_hanger.text_8: For a shorter hookup, enable Feed posts. Wire your supply to the positive and negative posts at the foot. Each feeds its matching overhead terminal.
powerdock.ponder.catenary_hanger.text_4: Set Height from 4 to 12 and Width from 3 to 13 blocks. The terminal box, crossbeam and ceramic mounts move together.
Choose a Cantilever pole or Square portal and start with Feed posts off.
Hold a stack of Insulated Copper Wire and sneak-right-click the pole or arm to fit the positive lead.
Repeat for the negative lead. Both leads run up to their matching terminals.
Use regular wire clicks to connect the supply to the matching positive and negative posts at the foot.
Right-click a lead or its clip with Power Grid Wire Cutters to remove just that lead.
powerdock.ponder.catenary_route.text_1: Hold bare Power Grid Copper Wire. Sneak-right-click either hanger to start from that end.
powerdock.ponder.catenary_route.text_2: Sneak-right-click the second hanger to preview both wires. The prompt shows that linking is active.
powerdock.ponder.catenary_route.text_3: To cancel, sneak-right-click into empty air away from the track.
powerdock.ponder.catenary_route.text_4: Sneak-right-click the previewed hanger again to confirm. Each span follows up to 64 blocks of track.
powerdock.ponder.catenary_branches.text_: Start with a main line. A single hanger can serve more than one branch.
When the rails offer more than one route, sneak-right-click a rail on the leg you want to mark a waypoint.
Preview the span to the siding hanger, then sneak-right-click it again to confirm.
Mark the other leg and link back to the main line to close the loop. Both routes can carry current.
To remove one route, sneak-right-click the highlighted rail with an empty hand to open Hanger Settings.
Use the arrows to highlight a span. Select Cut highlighted span and confirm. The main line stays connected.
powerdock.ponder.catenary_feeders.text_1: Use normal right-clicks with Power Grid wire to feed any hanger. Match positive to positive and negative to negative.
powerdock.ponder.catenary_feeders.text_2: More than one supply can feed the same line. How they share the load depends on voltage and wire resistance.
powerdock.ponder.catenary_feeders.text_3: Unequal supply voltages can push current back into the lower-voltage supply.
powerdock.ponder.catenary_feeders.text_4: Keep each supply, its wiring and its feeder hanger loaded. The line can carry power through intermediate chunks that unload.
powerdock.ponder.pantograph.text_1: Mount the pantograph along the carriage and connect its two posts to the onboard circuit.
powerdock.ponder.pantograph.text_2: Right-click with an empty hand to raise it. The contact bar follows both overhead wires.
powerdock.ponder.pantograph.text_3: At an insulated gap, the head stays raised while the onboard circuit disconnects.
powerdock.ponder.pantograph.text_4: The pickup reconnects automatically under the next powered section.
powerdock.ponder.pantograph.text_5: Sneak-right-click with an empty hand to open the receiver. Match both item slots to the cab's transmitting Redstone Link.
powerdock.ponder.pantograph.text_6: Turn the cab signal on to raise the pickup from inside the train.
powerdock.ponder.pantograph.text_7: Turn the signal off to lower it and disconnect power.
powerdock.ponder.power_dock.text_1: Mount facing Power Docks on two Sable craft, or put one on a fixed station.
powerdock.ponder.power_dock.text_2: Wire Positive and Negative into the local circuit on each side. The docks join matching posts in parallel.
powerdock.ponder.power_dock.text_3: Arm both docks with redstone and bring the craft together slowly.
powerdock.ponder.power_dock.text_4: As the heads meet, the amber lamps light. Power can flow either way and a comparator reads 15.
powerdock.ponder.power_dock.text_5: Turn off either dock to open the circuit, retract the arms, and release that pair.
powerdock.ponder.deck_rail_jumper.text_1: Mount the Deck Rail Jumper on an open Loconautics deck. Point the cord outlet at the next car.
powerdock.ponder.deck_rail_jumper.text_2: Match the outlet to a knuckle that faces the same way. Corner mounts work when the next car has a matching jumper.
powerdock.ponder.deck_rail_jumper.text_3: Wire the two copper posts on top to the car's Power Grid circuit. Keep Positive and Negative matched.
powerdock.ponder.deck_rail_jumper.text_4: With CC: Tweaked, place a Networking Cable directly above the socket to join the cars' wired networks.
powerdock.ponder.deck_rail_jumper.text_5: When the knuckles couple, the cord connects power and optional data. The amber lamp shows the connection.
powerdock.ponder.deck_rail_jumper.text_6: The cord flexes as the coupled cars turn and climb.
powerdock.ponder.deck_rail_jumper.text_7: Uncouple the knuckles to retract the cord and disconnect both circuits.
powerdock.ponder.flush_rail_jumper.text_: Fit the Flush Rail Jumper into a Loconautics end wall. Install it from inside, facing the next car.
Match the outlet to a knuckle that faces the same way. Corner mounts work when the next car has a matching jumper.
Wire both copper posts from inside the car. The power posts and the square data socket share the inside face.
With CC: Tweaked, put a Networking Cable directly against the inside socket. The cord comes out on the other side of the wall.
When the knuckles couple, the cord connects power and optional data. The amber lamp shows the connection.
The cord flexes as the coupled cars turn and climb.
Uncouple the knuckles to retract the cord and disconnect both circuits.
